clue.text: Publicity favoured by board as OK for publication

parts.note: PR, short for public relations, means publicity
to be in is to be in favour, popular
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A notice backed by the company board is cleared to be printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fit to appear in print without offence is acceptable for publication.

clue.text: Saint creates trouble ignoring society leader

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving a letter out of the word

parts.note: to pester is to trouble or harass

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word society

explanation.surface: A holy figure causes a nuisance and snubs a high-society figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Peter was the leading apostle, venerated as a saint.

clue.text: Nice art — it could be ornate

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Art from Nice may be decorative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, its capital hiding that it is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate means elaborately detailed, much as ornate does.

clue.text: Difficult demand, later relaxed, to imprison master

indicators.note: to imprison puts the master inside the rearranged letters
relaxed means loosened, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: a lord is a master

explanation.surface: A tough order, eased later, to lock up the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficult demand' reads like a description of the clue's own instruction, but it is the definition; 'relaxed' shuffles the letters and 'to imprison' wraps them round the master.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is an idiom for a request that is hard to fulfil.

clue.text: Must one sink to this to get a good deal?

definitions.text: Must one sink to this to get a good deal?

parts.words: Must one sink to this to get a good deal?
parts.note: sinking is both lowering oneself and going down to the lowest floor of a shop, where cut-price goods are sold

explanation.surface: Must one stoop this low for a bargain?
explanation.definitionFit: A store's lowest floor, where cheap goods are sold, is where bargains are found.

clue.text: Admiral disconcerting a lot at Number Ten

indicators.note: disconcerting means throwing into confusion, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A naval chief greatly unsettles the Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: Number Ten Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's home, a natural place for politics, but here only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Mountbatten, the 1st Earl, was Admiral of the Fleet and First Sea Lord.

clue.text: Horse about to go over again

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for the horse is read backwards

parts.note: a pacer is a horse bred for harness racing at the pace

explanation.surface: A horse is about to cover the same ground again.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise, going over the main points once more.

clue.text: Stir when author's introductory page is cut

indicators.note: is cut means the letter is removed from the author's name

parts.note: Marcel Proust was the French novelist

indicators.note: introductory means the first letter of page

explanation.surface: A fuss arises when a writer's opening page is trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to stir up or rouse someone, as from bed.

clue.text: Firm embracing left-wing set of beliefs

indicators.note: embracing means holding around, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
red means left-wing, socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A company adopts a socialist manifesto.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, a statement of beliefs.

clue.text: Carried in piece of metal to be inserted into socket

indicators.note: in places the carrying word within the metal piece

parts.note: a pin is a small piece of metal
lugged means carried with effort

explanation.surface: A metal part is carried in to be fitted into a power point.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance plugged in has its plug inserted into a socket.

clue.text: Like certain churches taking minimal time with strange ritual

parts.note: T, the shortest abbreviation for time

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of the next word are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Some churches hold a quick, peculiar ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: In Rome the titular churches are those assigned to cardinals, each cardinal holding one as his title; 'strange' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Titular churches are the Roman churches attached by title to cardinals, so the adjective describes that class.

clue.text: Said to regret look produced by coil of ribbon

indicators.note: said signals that the words are spoken, and the sound is what matters

parts.note: to rue is to regret; lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: Someone claims to regret the appearance of a ribbon decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A rouleau is a roll or coiled trimming of ribbon, used in dressmaking and millinery.

clue.text: Beast foreign character keeps at home

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
in means at home

explanation.surface: A creature that a foreign person keeps in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhinoceros is a large horned wild animal, a beast of the savannah.

clue.text: A jolly powerful jazz musician

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, RM
strong means powerful

explanation.surface: A cheerful, forceful jazz player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective but is naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Armstrong was the celebrated jazz trumpeter and singer.

clue.text: Broken bit in river swallowed by fish

indicators.note: swallowed by puts the first piece inside the second

parts.note: the shad is a fish of the herring family
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A broken fragment in a river is gulped down by a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a broken fragment, especially of pottery or glass.

clue.text: Orderly's repeated "Silence! keeping one quiet, the brute

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the pair goes inside the doubled word
repeated means the word is given twice

parts.note: sh is a call for silence
I is the Roman numeral one
p, piano, means quiet in music
an ape is a brute

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly keeps hushing someone so the brute stays quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' looks like a hospital attendant but is an adjective; SH twice, SHSH, goes round I and P.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape means neat and in good order, like a well-kept vessel.

clue.text: Hours Enid cooked to get one properly fed

indicators.note: cooked means altered or fixed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Enid spent hours cooking to give somebody a decent meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' belongs to the kitchen picture but is the anagram signal on HOURS ENID.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well nourished means having been given the food needed for health.

clue.text: Cor, I'm nude running wild — such a lack of decency!

indicators.note: running wild suggests disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A gasp at someone streaking naked: what a lack of decency!
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is improper behaviour, a want of propriety.

clue.text: Argue aggressively? Sufferer with a rotten tooth might do that

definitions.meaning: to settle a dispute by open confrontation

definitions.text: Sufferer with a rotten tooth might do that
definitions.meaning: literally to get the bad tooth removed

explanation.surface: A row, or a trip to the dentist?
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to thrash out a quarrel and, literally, to have something removed.

clue.text: I will get man into my clutches?. Intoxicating!

indicators.note: into puts the man's name inside the other piece

parts.note: a net is what clutches its catch
Brian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A predator gloats over a man caught in its grip, finding it heady.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriant is something that intoxicates, used here as an adjective meaning intoxicating.

clue.text: Piece of furniture woman put at front of store's vehicle?

indicators.note: put at front of places the woman before the vehicle

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
a van is the vehicle a shop uses for deliveries

explanation.surface: A woman sits a sofa at the front of the shop's delivery van.
explanation.definitionFit: A divan is a low backless couch or bed, a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Angry no end about a bishop joining a TV series

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes round the next pieces
no end means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: sore means angry, in American usage
the Pope is the Bishop of Rome

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about a bishop appearing in a television drama.
explanation.walkthrough: SORE with 'no end' becomes SOR, which goes 'about' A POPE; the final A is the second 'a' in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama on television or radio.

clue.text: Work of art producing some embarrassment

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: An artwork that causes some awkwardness.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a rich tapestry, named after the French town of Arras.

clue.text: Ready to skate but held back?

explanation.surface: A skater poised but kept waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both on a frozen surface and, idiomatically, put on hold.

clue.text: Illness makes companion unwell

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: An illness strikes a friend down.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a mild feverish illness caught from cold.

clue.text: French river with American plant

parts.note: the Lot is a river in south-west France
US means American

explanation.surface: A French river has an American plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, a flowering plant.

clue.text: Transport business — something affected by recession in the East End?

indicators.note: in London's East End Cockneys drop the letter H at the start of words

parts.note: a hairline is what recedes as a man goes bald

explanation.surface: An airline company hit by an economic downturn in east London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' looks economic but means a receding hairline; the East End is the Cockney part of London, where the H is famously not sounded.
explanation.definitionFit: An airline is a company carrying passengers and freight by air, a transport business.

clue.text: Expel number of people coming to meeting

definitions.meaning: to ... someone is to throw them out

definitions.text: number of people coming to meeting
definitions.meaning: the attendance figure at an event

explanation.surface: A gathering ejects the people who came along.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to evict someone and the count of those who attend an event.

clue.text: Follow girl joining blokes without leader

indicators.note: without leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: blokes are men
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl tags along with some men who have no boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without leader' drops the first letter of the blokes, and 'joining' simply sets the girl alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on as a result or afterwards.

clue.text: Craftsmen who are money-makers?

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money
smiths are metalworkers who make things

explanation.surface: Which artisans earn the cash?
explanation.walkthrough: 'money-makers' suggests the rich or a mint, but tin is slang for cash and smiths are makers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsmiths are metalworkers who make and mend articles of tin plate, skilled workers.
